newsitem.title: USA: Consolidated Q1 hit by weather, overhead.
newsitem.headline: Consolidated Q1 hit by weather, overhead.

text.p: Consolidated Natural Gas Co Tuesday reported lower first-quarter profits, citing mild winter weather and higher marketing overhead costs.

The company reported profits for the first quarter of $171.5 million, or $1.81 a share, down from first-quarter 1996's $180.8 million, or $1.92 a share, the highest quarterly earnings in the company's history.
"Consolidated's broad performance improvement is not fully reflected in the reported results," said chief executive George A. Davidson Jr.
"Production of gas and oil was up, our average wellhead price for oil increased and our interstate pipeline and local distribution utilities turned in strong operating performances," Davidson said.

Excluding the effect of weather in both quarters and a special workforce reduction charge in 1996's first quarter, the company's earnings would have been $1.94 a share this year and $1.82 in first quarter 1996.
Pretax operating income for exploration and production was $38.3 million, up six percent from $36.2 million.

Late in the quarter, the company said, two big projects in the Gulf of Mexico began production: the Neptune deepwater oil project and West Cameron Block 631. The cost of bringing these and other projects on line increased operating expenses at CNG Producing Co somewhat, but per-unit production costs are expected to level off as the year goes by.

Natural gas production increased 15 percent to 36.3 billion cubic feet and oil production was up about 24 percent, to 1.2 million barrels. The average wellhead price for the oil production was up about 3 percent to $17.28 a barrel and natural prices were flat at $2.71 a thousand cubic feet.
Consolidated said the negative effect of warmer weather was most keenly felt by four local distribution utilities.
With weather that was 8 percent warmer than normal and 15 percent warmer than the first quarter of 1996, pretax operating income for the distribution component was down 16 percent to $172.4 million.

Pretax operating income for CNG's interstate gas pipeline and storage component was up 10 percent to $71.7 million. The improvement was due mainly to lower costs at CNG Transmission Corp and the settlement of certain regulatory issues.

CNG said its unregulated energy marketing services component had a pretax operating loss of $1.6 million during the first quarter, compared with a $1 million loss a year earlier. Marketed volumes of natural gas increased by more than two-thirds to 198.7 billion cubic feet while power sales more than tripled to 2.6 million megawatt-hours.
Higher overhead costs related to expanding the power marketing business were the primary reason for the larger loss, Consolidated said.
